sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-05

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Transverse US shows linear, bright hyperechoic foci caused by pneumobilia along the expected course of the biliary tree.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-06

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Longitudinal color Doppler US shows multiple echogenic stones within the common bile duct, causing upstream biliary ductal dilation . Color Doppler is helpful to distinguish avascular ducts from adjacent vasculature.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-07

sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-08

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Transverse color Doppler US shows several small, well-defined peribiliary cysts along the left portal vein .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-09

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Transverse US in a patient with hepatic schistosomiasis shows a thick, echogenic mantle of fibrotic tissue in the periportal area, encasing the portal veins . (Courtesy W. Chong, MD.)
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-10

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Transverse US in a patient with recurrent pyogenic cholangitis shows echogenic intrahepatic stones and sludge within moderately dilated intrahepatic biliary ducts. Note the periductal hyperechogenicity related to periductal inflammation.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-11

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Color Doppler US in the same patient shows no flow within the dilated intrahepatic duct , confirming the findings are indeed in the biliary tree rather than the portal or hepatic arterial system.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-12

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Transverse color Doppler US shows multifocal linear, branching, echogenic structures that are hepatic artery calcifications related to end-stage renal disease.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-13

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Longitudinal color Doppler US in a patient s/p cholecystectomy shows a cystic duct remnant appearing as a round, cystic lesion in the region of the porta hepatis.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-14

sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-01

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows dilated intrahepatic bile ducts due to carcinoma of the pancreatic head. The ducts lie on only one side (usually anteromedial) of the portal vein branches.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-02

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in a healthy 22-year-old woman shows a collar of low-density edema surrounding portal venous branches caused by overhydration following motor vehicle crash. Note distended inferior vena cava (IVC), also due to hypervolemia.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-03

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows a collar of low-density lymphedema surrounding portal venous branches due to IV hydration in an 18-year-old boy following trauma. Note distended IVC as an additional sign of overhydration and hypervolemia.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-04

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows a collar of low density surrounding the portal venous branches in a healthy 18-year-old boy who had aggressive IV fluid resuscitation following a motor vehicle crash.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-05

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in a 78-year-old woman with congestive heart failure shows periportal edema and a distended IVC .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-06

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows distention of the hepatic veins and IVC with perivascular edema in this 78-year-old woman with congestive heart failure.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-07

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in a 35-year-old man shows a collar of periportal lymphedema and porta hepatic lymphadenopathy due to acute viral hepatitis.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-08

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in the same patient shows marked gallbladder wall edema and a small amount of ascites.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-09

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows multiple hepatic abscesses with contrast-opacified walls. The abscesses were in communication with pus-filled ducts from ascending cholangitis.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-10

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: AP transhepatic cholangiography shows markedly irregular contour and arborization of the intrahepatic ducts and partial filling of abscess cavities .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-11

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows periportal edema , mild dilation of ducts , and a pyogenic abscess , all due to ascending cholangitis following Whipple resection for pancreatic carcinoma.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-12

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows periportal lymphedema and gas within mildly dilated ducts , plus a liver abscess , all due to ascending cholangitis following Whipple resection for pancreatic carcinoma.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-13

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Coronal MRCP shows irregular arborization of the intrahepatic ducts with a beaded appearance of some segments. In this 60-year-old man with ulcerative colitis and primary sclerosing cholangitis, portions of the left hepatic ducts are more dilated than the common duct.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-14

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T1 FS MR in the same patient shows low-intensity fibrosis paralleling the portal veins and mimicking dilated bile ducts.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-15

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: ERCP shows abnormal arborization of intrahepatic ducts that terminate abruptly . The common duct is dilated due to a stricture of the distal common bile duct .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-16

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Coronal T2 MR shows dilated bile ducts with the left lobe ducts dilated out of proportion to the right lobe. Within the dilated left lobe ducts, there are numerous and large filling defects, representing calculi .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-17

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T2 FS MR in an older Asian woman shows dilated intrahepatic bile ducts containing innumerable calculi . Recurrent pyogenic cholangitis can cause periportal edema in addition to massively dilated bile ducts.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-18

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in a 45-year-old Asian woman with recurrent bouts of cholangitis and sepsis shows grossly dilated bile ducts , some of which contain gas , plus a hepatic abscess .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-19

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Coronal oblique MRCP shows dilation and irregular arborization of the bile ducts and a stricture of the distal common bile duct due to AIDS-related cholangiopathy. Similar findings could be seen with primary sclerosing cholangitis.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-20

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows surgical clips from right hepatic lobectomy (for metastases). Irregular dilation of intrahepatic ducts is the result of hepatic intraarterial chemotherapy.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-21

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows moderate, irregular dilation of intrahepatic ducts from prior hepatic arterial chemotherapy.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-22

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows dilated intrahepatic ducts with indistinct walls due to biliary necrosis. Intrahepatic bilomas and ascites are also noted. These are classic signs of hepatic artery stenosis or thrombosis following liver transplantation.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-23

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows classic periportal edema that surrounds the portal venous branches. This is a common finding in recent liver transplant recipients and does not imply injury to the allograft.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-24

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in a 20-year-old woman injured in a motor vehicle crash shows the left lobe irregular laceration/hematoma with some blood tracking along portal vein branches.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-25

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in a 45-year-old woman with advanced cirrhosis shows cystic and tubular water-density structures that parallel the portal veins. These are biliary cysts, not dilated ducts.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-26

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T2 FS MR in the same patient shows another view of the cystic and tubular water-intensity lesions that parallel the portal veins and mimic dilated ducts.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-27

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows low-density, branching structures that mimic dilated bile ducts but represent occluded portal vein branches. Note collateral veins in this 58-year-old woman who had an autologous bone marrow transplantation prior to becoming hypercoagulable.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-28

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in the same patient shows a thrombosed right portal vein that might be mistaken for a dilated duct. Again, note collateral veins .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-29

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows mottled lucency in the liver, mostly in a perivascular distribution due to steatosis (fatty liver). Steatosis often favors the perivascular planes and "spares" the liver adjacent to the gallbladder fossa.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-30

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial arterial-phase CECT shows an enhancing tumor thrombus distending the main portal vein. Note the thrombosed right portal vein simulating dilated ducts and the enhancing hepatocellular carcinoma .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-31

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial MRCP shows dilation of intrahepatic ducts with obstruction near the confluence of the right and left main ducts due to cholangiocarcinoma . Malignant biliary obstruction may mimic or cause periportal edema.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-32

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T2 FS MR in a 66-year-old man with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) shows an infiltrative mass with intermediate signal intensity in a periportal distribution without venous invasion.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-33

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in the portal venous-parenchymal phase shows periportal hypoattenuation that encases and narrows the right portal vein. This was interpreted as cholangiocarcinoma, but surgical resection (right hepatectomy) showed only inflammatory pseudotumor of the liver and bile ducts.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-34

CORE_SOURCE_BASIS: junzi-shi-core-radiology-a-visual-approach-to.pdf (Core Radiology, Second Edition, 2021), Gastrointestinal Imaging; relevant printed GI pages 103, 109, 116, 121, 123-125, 139-144.
CORE_FACTS_USED:

* Viral hepatitis: when imaging is abnormal, periportal edema may produce a starry-sky ultrasound appearance and fluid on both sides of portal veins on CT/MRI; gallbladder-wall edema may coexist.
* Portal-vein thrombosis: lack of portal flow/echogenic thrombus; long-standing thrombosis produces multiple periportal collateral vessels (cavernous transformation).
* Pneumobilia is central branching gas; portal venous gas extends peripherally; both can be echogenic with dirty shadowing on ultrasound.
* Ascending cholangitis: bile-duct wall thickening/hyperenhancement with intraluminal debris and/or choledocholithiasis when abnormal.
* PSC: beaded irregular intra- and extrahepatic ducts; AIDS cholangiopathy can mimic PSC and more often includes papillary stenosis.
* Recent liver transplant: periportal edema can be a normal postoperative finding.
* Hepatic lymphoma can be infiltrative while preserving vasculature; it tends to be hypoechoic on ultrasound and hypoenhancing on CT/MRI.
* Cardiac hepatopathy: enlarged hepatic veins/IVC with reflux and mottled enhancement support passive congestion.
CORE_DERIVED_CARDS:
* High-Yield cards on acute viral hepatitis US and CT/MRI patterns.
* Boards Trap card separating pneumobilia from portal venous gas.
* UNKNOWN/support reasoning for cavernous transformation, passive congestion, hepatic lymphoma, PSC, ascending cholangitis, and post-transplant edema.
* High-Yield and Boards Trap cards on ascending cholangitis, post-transplant periportal edema, and periportal edema versus ductal dilation.
CORE_LIMITATIONS:
* Core does not provide a single standalone section titled Periportal Lesion; validation required synthesis across the liver, hepatic Doppler, transplant, and biliary sections.
* Periportal-specific details not explicitly present in Core were taken only from the supplied RadPrimer/STATdx master source.
* No external diagnostic-performance values were used.
